title: Developer Experience Documentation: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Fixes
author: Priya Desai
summary: Canonical guidance for Developer Experience (DevEx) content: standards and templates for SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and a prioritized list of top support issues with canonical fixes.
body:
Overview:

This document defines the structure, standards, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) content at Redwood Inference. It covers: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top customer support issues with canonical fixes. The goal is to make docs consistent, discoverable, and actionable for engineers integrating Redwood APIs and SDKs.

Audience:
- Software engineers and ML engineers using Redwood SDKs and APIs
- DevEx authors and maintainers
- Support engineers and solutions/SEs

Scope:
- Public-facing SDK guides: Python, JavaScript/Node, Go (internal variants exist for other languages)
- Quickstarts and templates used by self-serve onboarding flows and example repositories
- Canonical API examples (curl, Python, Node) kept in sync with SDK versions and released model catalog
- Docs site operating procedures: publishing flow, CI checks, review SLAs, deprecation process
- Top support issues and canonical fixes for the SDKs and API patterns

Ownership and Roles:
- Content owner: DevEx (eng-developer-experience)
- Primary author: Priya Desai
- Reviewers: Michael Chen (SDK lead), Laura Martinez (support lead)
- Maintainers: individual SDK owners (see SDK owner list in team wiki)

Standards and Conventions (must-follow):
- Titles: short, descriptive, kebab-case for filenames (e.g., python-sdk-quickstart-2026.json)
- Headings: use clear section headings and short intro paragraphs
- Code examples: include minimal, executable snippets for curl and SDKs; mark required env vars
- Quickstarts: complete end-to-end examples <5 minutes to run with free-tier/demo credentials
- Versioning: include SDK version and API compatibility in each guide (example: SDK v1.4 / API v2026-01)
- Review cadence: major guides reviewed quarterly; quickstarts and API examples reviewed on release or security change

Content taxonomy and file structure (logical):
- SDK guides: /eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides/{language}/{topic}  (e.g., authentication, streaming, function calling)
- Quickstarts & templates: /eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/{use-case}-{language}-quickstart
- API examples: /eng-developer-experience/api-examples/{operation}.{ext} and mirrored in example-repos
- Docs site ops: /eng-developer-experience/docs-site/{operating-procedure}  

SDK Guides: structure and required sections:
1) Short summary: what the SDK provides and when to use it
2) Prerequisites: supported SDK version, authentication, environment variables, network access
3) Installation: pip/npm/go get with exact package names and pinned versions
4) Minimal example: copy-paste runnable example (curl + SDK)
5) Common patterns: streaming, retries, pagination, batching, KV cache usage, rate-limiting guidance
6) Troubleshooting: mapping of SDK errors to API HTTP codes and recommended mitigations
7) API compatibility and changelog: link to model catalog and breaking changes

Example: Python SDK Quickstart (required content):
- Prereqs: Python 3.9+, pip, REDWOOD_API_KEY set in env
- Install: pip install redwood-inference==1.4.0
- Minimal example:
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1-large", prompt="Translate to French: Hello world")
print(resp.text)
```
- Notes: include guidance on streaming vs. blocking generate, default timeouts (10s), and recommended reconnect strategy for transient network failures.

Quickstarts and Templates: requirements and naming
- Quickstart goal: single-page README + runnable example that completes core scenario (authentication, single request, parse response)
- Template types: 
  - integration: minimal code to call generation/embeddings in an app
  - pipeline: multi-step example (embed -> search -> generate)
  - deployment: sample Dockerfile + k8s manifest for Dedicated/Private deployment patterns
- Naming convention: {use-case}-{language}-quickstart-{year}.json (e.g., embed-search-node-quickstart-2026.json)
- Template table (human-readable):
  - Name | Purpose | Path 
  - react-chat-quickstart | client-side chat example using Redwood API + streaming | /quickstarts/react-chat
  - embed-search-python | embeddings + vector store search | /quickstarts/embed-search-python
  - serverless-deploy-template | deploy to FaaS with autoscaling hints | /quickstarts/serverless-deploy

API Examples: canonical set and maintenance
- Every API surface (text generation, chat, embeddings, rerank) must have canonical examples in: curl, Python, Node (JS). Go is optional but recommended for core endpoints.
- Example format: short description, request, response sample, and troubleshooting notes. Keep examples under 80 lines of code.
- Example maintenance: update examples in the example-repo and docs in the same PR that updates SDK or API surface. CI will run lint and smoke tests.

Canonical curl example (Authentication + generation):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","prompt":"Summarize: Redwood Inference is a developer-first LLM platform."}'
```

Docs Site Operating Procedures (publish & review):
- Repo and CI: docs content lives in the docs repo under /content; PRs trigger CI checks: link-check, code-block lint, markdownlint, sample-snippet smoke tests.
- Publishing flow: author -> peer reviewer -> DevEx approver -> merge -> scheduled deploy (hourly). Emergency hotfixs deploy on merge with "hotfix" tag and notify #devex-alerts.
- Review SLA: docs must be micro-reviewed within 3 business days; major changes require a 7-day review window and a designated rollout plan.
- Deprecation policy: mark docs with a deprecation banner and remove after 90 days of deprecation notice. Update related pages and examples.
- Template maintenance: maintain a central templates directory with canonical readme, LICENSE, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, and usage notes. Each template includes a CHECKLIST.md that covers environment, secret handling, and cost warnings.
- Accessibility & localization: run accessibility audit for major guides and mark pages needing localization; prioritize translations for top 5 guides by traffic.

Docs CI checks (required):
- link-check: no broken internal links
- code-snippet-smoke: run minimal snippet where safe (e.g., mocked API keys)
- lint: markdownlint rules and spelling checks (tech dictionary allowed)
- security-scan: detect accidental secrets or AWS keys

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (prioritized):
1) Authentication failures (401/403)
- Symptom: immediate 401 or 403 on first request after onboarding
- Common root causes: missing/invalid REDWOOD_API_KEY, key restricted by IP, or wrong environment variable name
- Canonical fix: confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY is set; run: `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY | wc -c` (must be >20). Verify key permissions in console and check IP restrictions. Owner: Support -> DevEx for docs update.

2) Streaming connection drops / partial responses
- Symptom: client receives truncated stream or connection resets during long responses
- Root causes: upstream network timeouts, load balancer idle timeout, or incorrect client-side timeout settings
- Canonical fix: increase client read timeout, enable reconnect + resume logic, and verify LB idle timeout >= 90s for streaming endpoints. Provide sample retry logic in SDK guide. Owner: SDK owners + Eng Platform.

3) Model mismatch / unexpected output format
- Symptom: app expects structured JSON but model returns text or different structure after model update
- Root causes: model variant changed (e.g., redwood-1-large -> redwood-1-large-2) or prompt format not explicitly constrained
- Canonical fix: pin model version in production, add response-schema checks, and use function/tool calling or structured-output features. Update quickstart prompts to include explicit output constraints. Owner: Applied ML & DevEx.

4) Rate limit (429) during bursts
- Symptom: intermittent 429s under burst traffic
- Root causes: client not respecting Retry-After header, missing exponential backoff, or misconfigured batching
- Canonical fix: implement exponential backoff with jitter, respect Retry-After, and batch requests where possible. Add sample backoff snippet in SDK guides. Owner: SDK owners + SRE.

5) Embedding drift / mismatch between indexed vectors and embeddings returned by SDK
- Symptom: reranking or semantic search returns poor results after model/quant changes
- Root causes: using different model for embedding generation vs. index creation, or forgetting to re-index after quant/approx change
- Canonical fix: enforce embedding model check in CI, include reindex step in deployment runbooks, and expose embedding model in index metadata. Owner: Applied ML + Search infra.

6) Local dev environment mismatch (TLS / mTLS / proxy)
- Symptom: requests succeed in prod but fail in developer laptop behind corporate proxy
- Root causes: missing proxy env vars, TLS inspection breaking websockets/streaming, or local firewall rules
- Canonical fix: document common proxy env vars (HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY / NO_PROXY), recommend using DevEx provided dev container, and provide instructions for bypassing TLS inspection for local testing. Owner: DevEx + Eng Infra.

Procedure for canonical fixes:
1) Triage and reproduce with minimal example
2) Draft a short KB article (one page) with reproducible steps and fix
3) Create/update SDK guide with code fix and add test case to docs CI if possible
4) Notify #support and #devex and add a short entry to the monthly support digest

Maintenance checklist for this doc (authors):
- Quarterly review of top issues and update canonical fixes (owner: DevEx)
- Run docs CI on all quickstart templates weekly to surface breaking examples
- After every SDK or API change, update examples in same PR or create a follow-up PR with high priority label

Related resources:
- SDK repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdks (internal)
- Example repos: github.com/redwood-inference/examples
- Docs CI playbook: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/developer-experience-docs-site-operating-procedures-2026

Appendix: Example backoff snippet (pseudo-code)
```python
import time, random
def backoff(attempt):
    base = 0.5
    cap = 10
    sleep = min(cap, base * (2 ** attempt)) + random.uniform(0, 0.1)
    time.sleep(sleep)
```

Contact and escalation:
- For doc pipeline failures: @devex (Slack channel #devex)
- For production-impacting doc regressions (broken quickstart causing customer impact): page-owner -> DevEx lead -> Eng Platform oncall (follow escalation playbook)

This page is the canonical operating playbook for Developer Experience content. Keep it current and treat examples as executable contracts with SDK and API owners.
